answer: Ripple pricing for join stamps: a new identity must submit a hash whose work is 2^20 times k/20, where k counts joins in the trailing hour, so each join costs more as the crowd grows and a burst of n joins costs about n squared over 40 base units. A farm of 100 pays about 250 units; a lone newcomer pays 0.05. Bypass: patience, since joining at 20 per hour keeps every stamp at base price; rented hardware also shrinks the cut. Check rule: anyone recounts k from ledger join times and verifies the hash, rejecting a stamp below its price; the ledge is k = 20 and copper is the base unit.
